# Counters

Every counter Cavalry has, from `counters.toml`, the single source ([ADR 0012](../decisions/0012-lay-out-the-counters-file.md)). The driver publishes each one in the [counters file](counters-file.md). A static counter is allocated when the file is created, in the record whose index is its id, and its label is its name. An instance counter is allocated per key when its instance is created, and its label is the name, a space, and the key's text as the doc column defines it. A `counter` never decreases while allocated; a `gauge` moves both ways. This page is generated by `scripts/gen-counters.py`: edit `counters.toml`, never this page, and `just lint-counters` fails when the two differ.

| Id | Name | Kind | Scope | What a change means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `counters.allocated` | gauge | static | Metadata records in the allocated state, this counter's own record included. |  |
| 1 | `counters.allocation_failed` | counter | static | Counter allocations refused because every record was in use: the counters file is full, and whatever needed the counter was refused with it. | The counters file is full and new publications and subscriptions are refused until a counter is freed: close what is not used; the capacity is fixed in this version. |
| 2 | `publication.position` | gauge | instance | The producer position of one publication's log buffer, written by the driver on its duty cycle from a load it makes at most once every two milliseconds, so at most two milliseconds behind the publisher (ADR 0022, ADR 0032); key: correlation id (i64), session id (i32), stream id (i32), little-endian; label text: the three in decimal, space-separated. |  |
| 3 | `publication.limit` | gauge | instance | The position up to which one publication may write: the slowest subscriber's position plus the publication window, written by the driver; key and label as publication.position. | If publication.position sits at publication.limit, a subscriber is slow or stopped: compare the subscription.position counters of the stream and look at that subscriber. |
| 4 | `subscription.position` | gauge | instance | How far one subscription has read one publication's stream, written by the subscriber after each poll with a release store; key: correlation id (i64), session id (i32), stream id (i32), little-endian; label text: the three in decimal, space-separated. | A subscription.position that does not move while publication.position does is a subscriber that stopped polling; its publisher will be back-pressured when it reaches the window. |

The driver's log names the client; rebuild or remove it. |

## State machines

Every state machine on the data plane registers its states and transitions in `counters.toml` too, and `just lint-counters` fails a transition that names no counter, a counter that is not of kind `counter` in the table above, a counter whose constant no code in the enum's crate names, or an enum whose variants are not the machine's states (CLAUDE.md, invariant 4). The enum that holds the states carries the comment `// state machine: <name>` on the line before its definition. The check fails closed: every enum under `crates/*/src` whose name is or ends in `State`, `Status` or `Phase` carries that comment, or `// not a state machine: <why>` with the reason no transition of it needs a counter, and `just lint-counters` names the file and line of one that has neither. Each machine is listed here with the counter every transition adds one to.

### `counters_record`

States: `unused`, `allocated`, `reclaimed`.

| From | To | Counter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unused` | `allocated` | `counters.allocations` |
| `reclaimed` | `allocated` | `counters.allocations` |
| `allocated` | `reclaimed` | `counters.freed` |

### `catalog_slot`

States: `empty`, `valid`, `invalid`, `deleted`.

| From | To | Counter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `empty` | `valid` | `recording.started` |
| `empty` | `valid` | `recording.start_failed` |
| `empty` | `valid` | `driver.registry_full` |
| `empty` | `invalid` | `recording.invalidated` |
| `valid` | `invalid` | `recording.invalidated` |
| `deleted` | `invalid` | `recording.invalidated` |

### `recording`

States: `starting`, `live`, `stopped`, `failed`.

| From | To | Counter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `starting` | `live` | `recording.started` |
| `starting` | `failed` | `recording.start_failed` |
| `starting` | `failed` | `recording.catalog_full` |
| `starting` | `failed` | `driver.registry_full` |
| `live` | `stopped` | `recording.stopped` |
| `live` | `stopped` | `recording.write_failed` |
| `live` | `stopped` | `log_buffer.rejected_frame` |
| `failed` | `stopped` | `recording.stopped` |

### `replay`

States: `starting`, `live`, `stopped`, `failed`.

| From | To | Counter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `starting` | `live` | `replay.started` |
| `starting` | `failed` | `replay.start_failed` |
| `starting` | `failed` | `driver.registry_full` |
| `starting` | `failed` | `driver.log_create_failed` |
| `live` | `stopped` | `replay.stopped` |
| `live` | `stopped` | `replay.ended` |
| `live` | `stopped` | `replay.not_connected` |
| `live` | `stopped` | `replay.failed` |
| `live` | `stopped` | `log_buffer.rejected_frame` |

### `publication_connection`

States: `disconnected`, `connected`.

| From | To | Counter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `disconnected` | `connected` | `publication.connected` |
| `connected` | `disconnected` | `publication.disconnected` |

### `channel`

States: `initializing`, `active`, `closing`, `errored`.

| From | To | Counter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `initializing` | `active` | `channel.opened` |
| `active` | `closing` | `channel.closed` |
